recommended_title: Adaptive ILR Ellipsoids: Coverage–Volume Trade-offs on the Simplex
central_question: When does training-adaptive residual geometry improve the joint-coverage versus common-simplex-volume trade-off of split-conformal prediction regions for strictly positive compositional regression, and where does it fail?
central_thesis: In the tested synthetic regimes, externally calibrated adaptive ILR ellipsoids markedly reduce simplex-volume fractions under heteroskedastic logistic-normal responses, but nearly fill the simplex for near-boundary Dirichlet responses and remain below nominal coverage under covariate shift, so their empirical value is condition-dependent rather than uniformly superior.
narrative_rationale: The strongest evidence is the frozen four-fold residual model evaluated against two evaluator-owned baselines on five final seeds, not the order in which three training configurations were explored. The common-volume measurement exposes a meaningful reversal: the adaptive model is much smaller in the heteroskedastic regime but substantially larger than the Euclidean comparator in the boundary and shifted regimes. Separate marginal coverage, descriptive subgroup coverage, and volume rather than letting an aggregate selection utility conceal these trade-offs. This supports a standalone empirical methodology study with explicit negative results, not a new conformal validity theorem or a comprehensive geometry benchmark.

The inspected evaluator supplies valid Euclidean-simplex and isotropic-ILR comparators and six condition blocks; these are four synthetic regimes plus two matched interventions derived from the heteroskedastic regime, not six independent datasets.

The independent final evaluation is completed and qualified, grounded in final.qualification.status and final.qualification.outcome. Its qualification is not a nominal-coverage or superiority guarantee; the final evidence must still disclose undercoverage, volume failures, and missing diagnostics.

method_groups.name: Euclidean-simplex split-conformal balls
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned ridge predictions in composition coordinates, clipped and renormalized, with Euclidean residual calibration and simplex-intersected membership; essential because adaptive ILR does not dominate this comparator in volume.

method_groups.name: Isotropic ILR split-conformal balls
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned ridge locations in ILR coordinates with an unscaled residual norm; isolates a meaningful coordinate-space reference using the same external calibration and simplex-volume measure, without claiming a matched-training-size mechanism ablation.

method_groups.name: Four-fold residual adaptive ILR ellipsoids
method_groups.include_reason: Frozen selected model and sole adaptive method with released final evidence; describe as the studied configuration rather than an established novel algorithm or universal winner.

method_groups.name: Single-split residual adaptive ILR ellipsoids
method_groups.include_reason: Three search-seed measurements support a limited direct comparison with the four-fold configuration; the change bundles residual fitting, full-data location refitting, and training-data allocation, so it cannot identify a pure cross-fitting effect.

method_groups.name: Continuously interpolated covariance ellipsoids
method_groups.include_reason: Three search-seed measurements test continuous covariance interpolation against hard routing while retaining four-fold residual fitting; show no established advantage and keep this auxiliary branch out of the central thesis.

results_focus: Primary final comparison: show nominal 90% joint coverage and normalized common-simplex volume separately for the frozen adaptive model and both baselines in all six conditions, with four regimes visually separated from the two matched controls.

Heteroskedastic logistic-normal evidence: final five-seed means are coverage 0.904375 and volume 0.147566 for adaptive ILR, versus 0.903021/0.333621 for Euclidean and 0.903438/0.335896 for isotropic ILR; smaller measured sets at similar observed marginal coverage, not proven population dominance.

Boundary and shift limitations belong in the main results: near-boundary volume is 0.975856 versus 0.715514 for Euclidean; shifted coverage is 0.863281 versus 0.859219 for Euclidean and 0.708177 for isotropic ILR. The adaptive model has larger shifted volume than Euclidean (0.622107 versus 0.192813), so coverage and efficiency must be interpreted jointly.

Final equal-weight summary is coverage 0.894158 and volume 0.544618. Adaptive-minus-baseline coverage differences are -0.001441 for Euclidean and +0.025052 for isotropic ILR; baseline-minus-adaptive volume differences are -0.034631 and +0.049603 respectively. This average includes the two C2-derived controls and is not a broad population estimate.

Use the released paired seed-bootstrap intervals only for the equal-weight six-condition contrast they estimate: coverage versus Euclidean [-0.006536, 0.003854], volume reduction versus Euclidean [-0.054606, -0.011514], coverage versus isotropic ILR [0.018516, 0.031884], and volume reduction versus isotropic ILR [0.030559, 0.061766]. They are exploratory five-seed intervals, not multiplicity-corrected generalization guarantees or per-condition intervals.

Subgroup reliability: plot the evaluator’s four overlapping covariate-sign strata for heteroskedastic and shifted conditions. Training boundary tertiles and evaluation sign strata are different objects. Preserve the reported worst-stratum summary of 0.0 and explain that empty negative-sign strata in the constant-input control were encoded as zero; never call that an observed zero-coverage subgroup.

Auxiliary search comparison: compare three configurations directly on common search seeds 101, 211, and 307, separate from final seeds 1009, 2027, 3049, 4051, and 5059. Show coverage and volume, not a best-so-far trace. No final evaluation exists for the two auxiliary configurations in the released bundle.

Controls validate specific observed operations, not scientific superiority: constant covariates and training-pair derangement test information dependence; point-copy singleton and full-simplex checks anchor membership semantics; query-order invariance and replay check fixed predictions. Do not interpret their completion as conditional validity or real-data reliability.

planned_subsections.grounded_content: Transcribe the inspected selected fit_model: quadratic features for five covariates, four deterministic index-modulo folds, location ridge penalty 0.01, full-data refit, log residual-square offset 0.02 and ridge penalty 5, scale clipping [-6,5], standardized-residual clipping at 1000, pooled identity weight 8, group shrinkage weight 32, right-sided tertile routing, and the fewer-than-four-row fallback.
